items.remediation: Require synchronizer tokens or equivalent origin-bound intent signals for ambient-credential actions, validate Origin, choose purpose-appropriate SameSite, and use step-up for critical operations.
items.safety: Use a reversible mutation on a synthetic object and restore it immediately.

items.title: Distinguish CORS response access from CSRF request impact
items.objective: Determine whether testing correctly separates browser permission to read a response from the ability to send a state-changing request.
prerequisites: A designated test account and controlled cross-site origin
A reversible sensitive action or owner-approved stopping point
steps: Capture the normal request for a controlled cross-site request and its observable server state
Identify ambient credentials, token, Origin/Referer, SameSite, method, and media-type defenses
Build one browser-valid cross-site request changing only the defense under test
Verify authoritative state, restore it, and repeat a clean control

examples.note: Use a controlled cross-site page and reversible action only. Target: a controlled cross-site request and its observable server state.

items.manipulate: a controlled cross-site request and its observable server state, changing one anti-forgery signal or browser request shape at a time
items.secure_behavior: The browser request is rejected unless it carries a validated attacker-unavailable intent signal appropriate to the action.
items.vulnerable_behavior: the action commits even though JavaScript cannot read the response, or sensitive data is readable through a separate CORS flaw
items.validation: Reproduce in a real browser with actual cookie/token behavior and confirm committed server state; Repeater success or a 200 response alone is insufficient.
false_positives: missing ACAO does not prevent simple requests
permissive ACAO alone does not prove a state change or credentials

items.title: Require step-up or transaction binding for critical cross-site-reachable actions
items.objective: Determine whether high-impact actions rely only on a generic CSRF token instead of recent authentication and action-specific confirmation.
prerequisites: A designated test account and controlled cross-site origin
A reversible sensitive action or owner-approved stopping point
steps: Capture the normal request for an owner-defined critical action stopped before irreversible commit
Identify ambient credentials, token, Origin/Referer, SameSite, method, and media-type defenses
Build one browser-valid cross-site request changing only the defense under test
Verify authoritative state, restore it, and repeat a clean control

examples.note: Use a controlled cross-site page and reversible action only. Target: an owner-defined critical action stopped before irreversible commit.

items.manipulate: an owner-defined critical action stopped before irreversible commit, changing one anti-forgery signal or browser request shape at a time
items.secure_behavior: The browser request is rejected unless it carries a validated attacker-unavailable intent signal appropriate to the action.
items.vulnerable_behavior: a stolen/reused generic intent token is sufficient without required step-up or transaction detail binding
items.validation: Reproduce in a real browser with actual cookie/token behavior and confirm committed server state; Repeater success or a 200 response alone is insufficient.
false_positives: ordinary low-risk changes do not require transaction signing
a valid recent high-assurance session can satisfy documented policy
